Subject: Locality assurance and legal-hold exemptions

Evelyn / Laura,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're moving toward finalizing our Dedicated deployment and have two items the legal and procurement teams need clarified before we proceed:

1) Data locality assurance: we need a short written confirmation that tenant compute and persistent storage for our Dedicated pool will remain within the US region(s) we select, and that automated replication to other regions is disabled by default for our tenant.

2) Deletion vs. legal hold: our legal team says they may place legal holds on subsets of records at an account level. We need to understand how Redwood treats deletions for data under legal hold. Specifically: does a legal hold block automated tenant-scope deletion workflows? If so, what is the expected operator workflow and what proof can you provide that a delete did not occur while a hold was active?

Can you point us to an operations document or provide an attestation we can include in our contract? If helpful, Gina from legal is copied on this thread.

Appreciate a quick reply or a 30-minute sync later this week.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Senior IT Procurement, Acme Health

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short summary (redwood-locality-summary.pdf) for procurement/legal review.

- Data locality: for Dedicated deployments we provide a tenant-bound hosting model. By default we pin tenant data and persistent volumes to the customer-selected cloud region(s) and do not configure cross-region replication for tenant storage or KV caches. Backups/snapshots are also stored in the same region unless the customer opts into cross-region archival.

- Replication controls: we can provide a configuration lock that prevents operator-initiated replication for your tenant; that is part of the Dedicated onboarding checklist.

- Deletion + legal hold: Redwood honors customer legal holds. When a hold is placed we tag affected objects and block automated scrubbing workflows for those objects. The normal tenant-scope deletion flow will surface hold markers and will not remove items until the hold is lifted. Operator actions to override a hold require documented approval from two named customer contacts and are logged.

- Evidence and attestation: we can deliver an ops attestation package that includes (a) retention/hold event logs, (b) snapshot movement history, and (c) an auditable list of deletion attempts that were blocked due to holds.

Next steps:
1) I attached a short summary for procurement (redwood-locality-summary.pdf).
2) Aditya / Ben — can you review and confirm the attestation artifacts we can provide for Acme? I can then draft a short clause for inclusion in the MSA or SOW.
3) Sanjay / Gina — happy to book a 30-minute sync; my availability Wed 4/7 10–12 PDT.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart

Aditya's proposed additions for the attestation:
- Include a signed checklist that maps each retention class to the exact storage path (region, cluster id, disk ids) and dates when snapshots were written.
- Provide a redacted log extract showing the hold tag being applied and showing the subsequent blocked delete attempts (timestamps and operator ids).
- Add a line about the operator approval workflow (two named contacts) and include the verification steps we execute before any manual override.
- Propose a short attestation document we can sign via DocuSign that reads as: "Redwood Inference attests that Acme Health tenant data was stored only in the US region(s) selected and that deletions were blocked during periods where a customer-initiated legal hold was active."

Sanjay / Gina — thanks for the patience. Per Aditya and Ben's input, attached is our proposed attestation language and the ops artifact list (ops-attestation-draft.docx). Highlights below and suggested next steps.

Highlights:
- Region assurance: Redwood confirms that for the Acme Health Dedicated deployment tenant storage (persistent volumes, snapshots, and KV cache hotstores) will be confined to the US region(s) you select at provisioning. No cross-region replication will be enabled without express written consent.

- Legal hold behavior: when a legal hold is applied by an authorized Acme contact, affected objects are tagged and prevented from being removed by automated retention or tenant-scope deletion processes. Any manual override requires signed approval from two named Acme contacts and is logged with timestamps and operator identifiers.

- Evidence package: upon request we will provide a time-bound evidence package containing (i) redacted hold event logs, (ii) snapshot write and movement history showing region placement, (iii) deletion attempt audit entries, and (iv) a signed attestation PDF.

Suggested next steps:
1) Please review the attached ops-attestation-draft.docx and the redwood-locality-summary.pdf in the Drive link I sent.
2) If the language looks good we will convert to a short attestation PDF and send via DocuSign for signature. Link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=example123
3) If you want additional artifacts (e.g., disk IDs or full unredacted logs) we can scope that under an evidence request and a limited NDA/forensic access process.

If that works, I can send the DocuSign package today so procurement can sign off.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
